member.title: INTELLIGENT IMAGE-TO-TEXT AND STUDY NOTE GENERATION
member.overview: The image-to-notes component enhances handwritten images, extracts Sinhala text, translates the result into Tamil and English, and collects corrected OCR crops for future model training. The FastAPI CPU application invokes independent Modal enhancement, OCR and translation endpoints and returns text, line information and comparison images to an Expo interface.
member.purpose: The deployment supports evaluation of handwritten-image processing as a usable biology learning aid. Its purpose is to validate model connectivity, accepted upload handling, OCR cleanup, translation completeness, feedback retention and interface integration without treating optional correction agents as active in the current route.

blocks: The image-to-notes component enhances handwritten images, extracts Sinhala text, translates the result into Tamil and English, and collects corrected OCR crops for future model training. The FastAPI CPU application invokes independent Modal enhancement, OCR and translation endpoints and returns text, line information and comparison images to an Expo interface.

The repository contains a FastAPI CPU API, an Expo/React Native interface, Modal model definitions, and OCR cleanup tests. No component-specific Dockerfile, production hosting manifest, or root release workflow was found. The hosting procedure below is proposed from the supplied code; it does not certify an existing public deployment.

The interface imports `@/lib/api`, but `frontend-rn/lib/api` is absent from this checkout. Its API implementation and production URL configuration must be restored or implemented before frontend release. An `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` mechanism cannot be assumed from the current source.

The deployment supports evaluation of handwritten-image processing as a usable biology learning aid. Its purpose is to validate model connectivity, accepted upload handling, OCR cleanup, translation completeness, feedback retention and interface integration without treating optional correction agents as active in the current route.

A repeatable deployment must connect the interface, application services, model inference and persistent data while retaining the configuration and evidence required to reproduce the release. The assessment therefore considers both installation correctness and the learner-facing workflow.

This report covers the intelligent image-to-text and study note generation component only. The shared learning interface, research website and other three research components retain their own deployment responsibilities. The scope includes environment preparation, model endpoint configuration, application release, secure service access, verification, backup and recovery.

The report is based on the inspected project repository. Hosting already documented in source is identified separately from proposed installation steps. No new cloud release, paid inference or production database migration was executed during preparation. Runtime acceptance results require a release-specific evidence record.

The following metrics define the operational monitoring plan for deployment evaluation. They are selected from the component workflow and should be collected during a controlled acceptance run; measured values are not supplied in the available deployment evidence.
Root API response and successful enhancement/OCR/translation calls.
Cold/warm model duration and total image processing time.
Sinhala text, line confidence/crops, enhancement image and both translations.
Retained corrections, supported media types, rejected oversized inputs and disk growth.

Deployment success is evaluated against installation, integration and learner workflow criteria. Health checks alone are insufficient because an API can answer a liveness request while a model, database, index or private storage service remains unavailable.
Required processes start with the selected environment and no unresolved startup failure.
Frontend origin, API URL, model endpoints and persistent paths match the release record.
All mandatory component scenarios produce the expected outcomes.
Required learner state and files remain available after a controlled restart.
A compatible previous release and tested backup procedure are identified.

For a release trial, calculate deployment success rate as successfully verified required services divided by all required services, multiplied by 100. Calculate workflow error rate from failed requests divided by total observed requests over the same recorded test interval. Keep configuration failures, model failures and invalid-input rejections separate so that expected rejection behavior is not mistaken for an outage.

No measured deployment percentage or incident trend is asserted here. The release record must identify the test period, number of requests, endpoint/model revisions, and observed failures before reporting quantitative results.

The repository review establishes the component architecture, required configuration, release dependencies, verification scenarios and recovery requirements. A completed deployment should demonstrate a usable intelligent image-to-text and study note generation workflow and durable handling of the component data described below. Operational success remains subject to the acceptance criteria and pending items identified in this report.

The deployment process follows environment preparation, initialization, application/model release, access configuration and scenario-based verification. The steps are specific to this component and preserve its actual hosting and storage architecture.
Independent static web deployment after validated export

The source filename `srcnn_app.py` is historical: the current model implementation is Swin2SR. In the current `/api/process` route, enhancement is generated for comparison/download, while OCR receives the original image bytes to preserve handwriting characteristics. OCR output is cleaned and translated sequentially. SinhaLM/Qwen visual correction is skipped in this active route and the response sets `context_improved` to false. Additional agent files are optional deployments, not prerequisites for the current main processing path.

Select the release commit and install dependencies in an isolated environment. Record the actual operating system, runtime versions, host allocation, storage mapping and public endpoints. CPU/RAM specifications and concurrent-user capacity should be taken from the selected host and measurements rather than assumed from the presence of deployment scripts.

The CPU backend loads endpoint URLs and allowed origins from its environment. The current /api/process route creates enhancement output for comparison but sends the original image bytes to line-level TrOCR extraction. It then cleans Sinhala output and translates it sequentially. SinhaLM/Qwen visual context correction is skipped by this route. A writable persistent backend/dataset directory is needed when retaining learner corrections.

Configure application and model services using the following repository-supported variables and deployment sequence. Commands use a Linux deployment shell unless a PowerShell helper is explicitly identified.

Use an isolated Python environment and `backend/requirements.txt`. GPU dependencies are installed in Modal images rather than the CPU backend. Validate a clean frontend install against the checked-in package/lock files and Expo runtime before selecting a build image.

The model definitions reference `sarmisarmitha/swin2sr-sinhala-image-enhancement`, `sarmisarmitha/trocr-sinhala-handwritten-ocr`, and `facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M`. Confirm access to all referenced artifacts, including the TrOCR subfolder defined in source, before building the Modal images.

1. Record the release commit. Restore the frontend API module with upload/request handling, response types, and explicit configurable HTTPS backend origin. Match `/api/process` and error responses; do not hardcode a learner-device localhost address into the production client.
2. Authenticate Modal and deploy the active model services from `backend/`:

modal deploy modal_functions/srcnn_app.py
modal deploy modal_functions/trocr_app.py
modal deploy modal_functions/translate_app.py

Record the printed function URLs separately. Configure both TrOCR text and line URLs where required; `/api/process` specifically uses `TROCR_LINES_MODAL_URL`. Enhancement and TrOCR have 300-second scaledown windows in source. Cold-start acceptance must be measured separately from warm inference.
3. Prepare the CPU API environment from `backend/`:

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

Populate `.env` from `.env.example`, using the deployed URLs and exact frontend origins. Mount a writable persistent directory at `backend/dataset` if feedback retention is required. The feedback module creates the image directory during import, so directory permissions are a startup requirement.
4. Configure a process manager to run the API behind an HTTPS reverse proxy:

A single worker is the initial choice because feedback appends to a local JSONL file and uses timestamp-derived crop names; concurrent multi-worker dataset writing has not been established as safe. Set proxy upload limits and request timeouts to accommodate the configured image limit and measured multi-model processing duration.
5. After restoring the frontend module and its public configuration, run from `frontend-rn/`:

npm ci
npx tsc --noEmit
npx expo export --platform web

Host the successfully exported web directory, normally `dist/`, with HTTPS and routing compatible with the generated Expo export. No web hosting manifest is supplied in this component. Validate web deployment first; native Android/iOS distribution requires separate build/signing configuration and is not evidenced by this repository's deployment setup.

The hosted browser interface and API require compatible HTTPS endpoints and exact permitted frontend origins. Private credentials belong in the backend or deployment-secret store. Public frontend variables may contain the API origin and public identity key, but must not contain database passwords, service-role credentials or private deployment tokens.

Restrict internal process and database/index ports to the required application network. Access control must match the intended audience and be verified independently of CORS. Record how an administrator inspects logs and restarts the service using the tools selected for this component.

Execute the following component-specific scenarios using isolated test accounts, representative source material and a recorded release configuration. The descriptions are acceptance procedures, not claims that the scenarios have already passed.
Test procedure: Submit a representative accepted image to /api/process and inspect returned images and line-level text.
Expected behavior: OCR uses original image bytes and returns cleaned Sinhala output with comparison data.
Evidence to retain: request/test identifier, relevant screenshot or response, timestamps, service/model version and the observed pass/fail outcome.
Test procedure: Process a meaningful Sinhala sample and inspect both translation fields, including a controlled translation failure.
Expected behavior: Both translations contain usable output when their service succeeds; empty fields are detected during acceptance.
Evidence to retain: request/test identifier, relevant screenshot or response, timestamps, service/model version and the observed pass/fail outcome.

Test procedure: Save an isolated crop correction through /api/feedback/ocr, then restart and inspect images and metadata.

Evidence to retain: request/test identifier, relevant screenshot or response, timestamps, service/model version and the observed pass/fail outcome.

Monitor enhancement/OCR/translation errors, cold starts, request duration, dataset disk usage, missing URLs, and model build/download failures. Persist feedback images and `dataset/metadata.jsonl` together. Store dataset backups privately and confirm they can be restored.

The inspected routes do not enforce application authentication. Before deployment to an intended authenticated audience, implement or configure the required access control and test it. CORS alone does not prevent direct API calls. Configure upload/request protection according to that audience rather than assuming the Expo client provides backend access control.

Retain the previous API/client build, model source/revision references, and environment configuration. Roll back application code and compatible Modal endpoints independently, retaining the feedback dataset. Recheck a representative OCR request and translation pair after rollback. Model repositories are referenced by identifiers without an explicit immutable revision in the inspected definitions; record the resolved model revisions for reproducible releases.

Configuration and build gaps can prevent a usable client release even when individual backend services exist. Missing model artifacts or mismatched endpoints can interrupt inference, while incomplete persistence can cause learner state or feedback loss after restart. The listed actions address these concrete release dependencies. No outage duration, user count or production incident severity is inferred without a live record.

4. POST-DEPLOYMENT VALIDATION, DOCUMENTATION, AND LESSONS LEARNED

Post-deployment validation checks the integrated learning workflow after the selected release is installed. The procedure covers infrastructure, application dependencies, interface behavior and persistence. Validation should use representative learning material and controlled test state rather than modifying real learner records for convenience.
From the backend, run the existing cleanup checks:

Check `/` for API liveness and submit a representative Sinhala handwritten image to `/api/process`. Confirm original/enhanced images, cleaned Sinhala output, line crops/confidence, and Tamil/English fields are present. Translation failures are caught and can leave an empty translation field while processing otherwise succeeds; check translation content explicitly.

Test enhancement-only and OCR-only routes when included in the release. Test invalid media types, uploads above the configured limit, absent endpoint configuration, model errors, and CORS from the hosted client. The process route permits JPEG, PNG, WebP, and BMP content types; it does not establish support for arbitrary document/PDF uploads.

Submit a controlled correction to `/api/feedback/ocr`, verify its crop/metadata are saved, restart the API, and confirm persistence. Use an isolated dataset for acceptance so test corrections do not contaminate real training data. Check mobile/web upload behavior through the restored API client.

There is no dedicated `/health` or dependency-readiness endpoint in the inspected `main.py`. A successful `/` response only establishes that the API answers requests. Record end-to-end latency and OCR/translation behavior separately; no runtime pass results or quality metrics were collected for this report.
Inspect process/container status, HTTPS endpoint reachability, persistent mounts and startup logs.
Verify dependency configuration, model response handling, error behavior and the component-specific scenarios.
Validate the hosted production build, uploads/actions, result display and learner-visible failure behavior.
Restart services, confirm state retention, inspect access boundaries and verify compatible restoration.

Retain the source commit, runtime/package manifests, environment-variable names, deployment scripts/configuration, model identifiers, schema versions, test output and scenario evidence with the release. Store private environment values outside the published report. The editable report source and rendered PDF provide the documentation layer; application artefacts remain in the component directory.

Pending items include the missing frontend API module, validated Expo install/export, selected public hosts/URLs, persistent feedback storage, audience-specific access control, release automation, and live inference acceptance. SinhaLM/Qwen correction should only be described as active after the route is changed and validated.

The following lessons are derived from implementation and deployment review. They describe engineering implications of the available source, rather than unrecorded user trials or production performance claims.
Model filenames and comments can lag behind the active implementation; the enhancement service now uses Swin2SR.
A successful processing response does not guarantee complete translation output.
Feedback datasets require durable storage and release procedures that preserve training material.
A report should distinguish the installed architecture, planned checks and measured results so that later releases remain auditable.

The deployment review establishes a component-specific architecture, reproducible installation sequence, verification scenarios, monitoring plan and recovery requirements for intelligent image-to-text and study note generation. The identified pending items must be resolved and the acceptance evidence recorded before certifying a successful live deployment. The supporting documentation provides a reproducible operational basis for component evaluation and future releases.
